newsitem.title: TURKEY: Farm subsidies hurting Turk Ziraatbank finances - GM.
newsitem.headline: Farm subsidies hurting Turk Ziraatbank finances - GM.

text.p: State owned Ziraat Bank, Turkey's biggest bank which specialises in financing the agriculture sector, is troubled by the Treasury's delay in paying farm subsidies extended by the bank in the form of low-interest loans, its acting general manager Salih Sevki Doruk said.

"As the sole institution funding the agriculture sector... Ziraat Bank's financial structure is negatively affected by the deficit between low-interest farm loans and the cost of its funds," Doruk told a parliamentary commission.
"The Treasury does not pay in time and in cash (the loans) to the bank. Ziraat Bank's overdue receivables from the state were 384 trillion lira at end-October," Doruk said.
The last payment made by the Treasury for subsidies was 53 trillion lira provided to Ziraat at end-1995 in the form of special, five-year bonds.
Doruk said proper regulations were needed to prevent the delay in the Treasury's payments, adding that central bank's discount loans could be expanded to cover all of the subsidies.
He said 110 trillion lira of the low-interest loans were expected to be extended this year and bulk of them were financed from the bank's own sources.

Ziraat is the leading commercial bank with deposits totalling 1,100 trillion lira at end-October, compared to 542 trillion at the end of 1994. Its loans totalled 519 trillion lira at end-October, including 419 trillion of farm loans.
Ziraat's profit was 1.99 trillion lira last year.
